title: Reserve lattice + burst on-ramp packaging experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Design and validate a simplified packaging surface for Dedicated capacity that (1) low-friction on-ramps small-to-medium customers into reserved GPU commitments via a 'reserve lattice', and (2) offers bounded burst credits and autoscale guardrails to reduce support friction and overage churn.

Background: Sales and Solutions Engineering report frequent objections to long-term flat commits. Customers want predictable price / latency guarantees but also occasional burst headroom and simpler contract language. Existing offerings are numerous and produce negotiation friction. We need an experiment that combines a small number of SKUs with guardrails that enforce fair-use and predictable economics.

Hypothesis: A 3-tier reserve lattice (Starter / Growth / Anchor) plus a consumable surge-burst pool with explicit rate limits and pre-defined autoscale policy will increase closed-won conversion by 12-18% for mid-market opportunities and reduce dedicated overage disputes by 40%.

Scope:
- Design three packaged SKUs with commit bands, included surge credits, and autoscale policies.
- Define pricing math: base price per GPU-hour, committed discount, burst-credit unit price, overage smoothing rules.
- Produce contract addendum language for burst credits, preemption policy, and SLA crediting.
- Draft security questionnaire (SQ) responses for Dedicated + Private options covering data residency, KMS/HSM, audit logs and upgrade windows.
- Run a 4-week pilot with 4 sales opportunities (Mix of infra-heavy and latency-sensitive customers).

Out of scope: Single-tenant custom contracts (will be handled by enterprise motion), deep changes to runtime billing infra (engineering will be asked to instrument metering but not re-architect).

Top-line funnel metric: Sales conversion lift measured at pilot cohort within 30 days of contract signature.
measurement_plan: Primary: Pilot conversion rate (signed pilot -> paid tier) compared to matched historical control cohort.
Secondary: Overage disputes / billing tickets count for pilot customers vs baseline.
Operational: Accuracy of committed vs burst attribution (target <5% reconciliation variance at month-end).
Financial: Net ARR impact projection for 12 months under conservative vs aggressive price points.
SLO: No increase in p99 latency for serving tier after imposing autoscale guardrails.
pricing_matrix: Starter: 1-4 GPU commit bands, 20% discount vs on-demand, included 50 GPU-hours of burst credits per month, overage priced at 0.95x base on-demand rate.
Growth: 5-20 GPU commit bands, 30% discount, included 300 GPU-hours of burst credits, autoscale window up to 2x commit for 10 minutes bursts, overage smoothing applied in daily buckets.

Anchor: 21+ GPU commit bands, 40% discount, included 2,000 GPU-hours of burst credits, regional affinity, SLA credit ladder by reserved throughput bands. Enterprise negotiation allowed on top of list price.
Burst credits: consumable, non-refundable monthly pool that resets; unused credits do not roll over. Exception: pilot customers may receive one-time rollover for the first month.
Billing: Commit billed monthly in advance; burst credits consumed billed at month-end at discounted burst rate if pool exhausted; overage smoothing prorated by day to reduce billing spikes.
contract_notes: Addendum: Define 'burst credit' as a finite consumable pool with a usage meter and explicit exhaustion behavior.
Preemption: When capacity constrained, reserved workloads have priority; burst workloads may be preempted after a 2-minute grace period. Must be surfaced in docs and agreement.
SLA: SLA credit formula to be tied to reserved throughput bands (e.g., credit X% for Y minutes below reserved throughput over rolling 30-day window).
Data & Security: Include clauses for KMS integration, key ownership options for Private, and SOC2 / ISO references for higher-tier SKUs.
Audit & Support: Pilot customers to receive enhanced onboarding and a single point of contact; disputes escalation ladder included.
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: Finalize pricing matrix and legal addendum. Design one-page SKU brief and console mock for billing listing.
Week 2: Instrument metrics (engineering) and deploy analytics dashboard for pilot customers. Security to finalize SQ answers.
Week 3-6: Run 4-week pilot with selected customers. Collect usage, billing reconciliation, and sales feedback.
Week 7: Analyze results, update price points and contract language, and decide go/no-go for broader GA. Deliverables: playbook for Sales and SOW template for Pilot-to-GA conversions.
